title: Murdoch Wins Control of the News of the World After Maxwell Bid
description_short: On January 2, 1969, Rupert Murdoch won control of the News of the World after shareholders rejected Robert Maxwell’s Pergamon Press bid.
description_medium: On January 2, 1969, the BBC reported that shareholders backed the Carr family and Rupert Murdoch’s News Ltd. in the contest for the News of the World, defeating Robert Maxwell’s £34 million Pergamon Press offer. The earlier Guardian report described a planned 40% News Ltd. stake and joint management arrangement. Neither report links this newspaper deal to Donald Trump.
description_long: On January 2, 1969, the BBC reported that Rupert Murdoch had won control of the News of the World newspaper group after shareholders rejected a £34 million offer from Robert Maxwell’s Pergamon Press. The BBC account says the dispute began the previous October, when Pergamon made an initial £28 million offer, and that the Carr family joined News Ltd. in opposing it. A contemporary Guardian archive report dated October 25, 1968, had described News Ltd.’s planned 40% stake in the newspaper and said Murdoch was to become joint managing director with Sir William Carr. Together, these sources identify a British newspaper ownership contest over the News of the World; they do not support the supplied synopsis’s references to The Sun or “News Of The Times.” They also do not document any statement, action, or other event-specific connection to Donald Trump. The transaction can be described more accurately, but the Trump-focused inclusion question remains unresolved, so this proposed correction is held pending evidence of a Trump nexus or an explicit broader editorial scope.

The BBC reports that shareholders backed Murdoch and the Carr family after Robert Maxwell’s Pergamon Press made a £34 million offer, and says the contest began with an offer the previous October.
